title: Quick Accent browser malfunction associated with ESET keyboard protection

status.label: External keyboard-protection interaction
status.detail: The discussion identifies ESET and links a separately reported Quick Accent allowlist workaround; this issue itself remains open.

next_action.label: Summarize vendor-policy workaround
next_action.reason: Preserve the tested allowlist evidence without recommending security protection be disabled.

judgment.rationale: The author reproduced the problem with other applications, identified ESET keyboard protection and linked an executable-specific allowlist success. No PowerToys-specific failing code path is established.
evidence: Original 0.68/0.68.1 report affects Chrome and Edge but not Brave and lists ESET NOD32.
The author later states the problem affects other apps too, not just PowerToys.
Another affected commenter confirms ESET; the author identifies Safe Banking & Browsing keyboard protection.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/31787#issuecomment-2374115371 reports that allowing PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe in ESET Browser protection fixes the problem.
The final author comment links that workaround but explicitly says they have not tested it themselves.
judgment.recommended_action: Offer a vendor/IT-approved executable allowlist as a reported workaround, without claiming universal resolution or disabling browser protection.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current evidence places this interaction in ESET's protected-browser keyboard policy, including effects on other applications. A PowerToys code change is not justified by the reviewed evidence; vendor-approved configuration is the supported direction, not bypassing protection.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent shows characters for the wrong key in protected browsers; the discussion narrows this to ESET keyboard protection and links a successful executable-allowlist report.
known_information: Chrome and Edge behavior, versions and ESET presence are already supplied.
The author determined other applications were affected on the same machine.
A separate user reports success allowlisting PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe; the original author has not personally verified that workaround.
The issue is open and unassigned, despite its external-resolution title.
inferences: The evidence supports an external input-protection interaction, not a confirmed Quick Accent key-mapping defect.
issue_context.analysis: The ESET-presence question has already been answered. Do not ask it again or claim a merged PowerToys fix. Present the linked configuration result accurately and retain security/enterprise approval boundaries.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete report and eight comments, timeline and matching PR search.
Read the exact linked #31787 comment reporting the executable-specific allowlist result.

actions.label: Share reported ESET executable allowlist

comment.body: The discussion has narrowed this beyond Quick Accent: the original author observed the same browser problem with other apps, and affected users confirmed ESET. There is a reported executable-specific workaround here: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/31787#issuecomment-2374115371. That commenter says adding PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe to ESET's Browser protection allowlist fixed their issue. The original author here has not personally verified that workaround, so it is not a universal fix claim. Please consult ESET guidance or your organization's IT administrator before changing the allowlist; do not disable keyboard/browser protection as a workaround. Current evidence supports an external protected-browser input interaction rather than an identified PowerToys code defect.
